transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

You may not need a part at all, because a kinked hose or a blocked waste connection is usually fixed by straightening or clearing it. Whether you need one depends on what the next check finds, and without the model number I can't name a specific part. From what you have described, the most likely cause is blocked / kinked drain hose or waste connection. Next: Check the drain hose for kinks/crushing and the waste connection/standpipe for blockage (especially if the machine was recently moved). Let me know what you find.
hose behind looks OK, no kinks. sink drains fine too. the pump hums but nothing moves. so what part?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
It sounds like you'll most likely need a replacement drain pump, as a pump that hums without moving water usually has a jammed or failed impeller. The exact pump depends on your Bosch's model number, since different models use different pumps. The checks point to the drain pump. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
FD 9409 is what's on the sticker inside the door, I already gave you that. The line next to it is rubbed off so I can't read the rest. So which pump do I need?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
I can't tell you which pump you need yet. FD 9409 is only Bosch's production date code, and the pump is matched to the full model number (the E-Nr), which is the line that's been rubbed off. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drain pump obstructed / jammed or failed. With the filter out, shine a torch into the filter opening and gently turn the small plastic impeller (the vanes) with a finger. Does it turn freely, was anything caught in it, is it jammed, or do the vanes look broken?
ok did that. impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. also E18 came up on the display when it stalled.

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
E18 on your Bosch means: No drainage / drain took too long (clogged coin-trap/pump filter or drain hose). Next: Clear any trapped foreign object in the accessible pump path before recommending a replacement pump. Let me know what you find.
filter was already clean, just a bit of fluff. I can't get into the sump without tools and I'm not taking it apart. so is it the pump or not?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
It's very likely the pump: it hums without moving water, the impeller feels stiff and gritty, and you've already ruled out the filter, drain hose and sink. It isn't certain, though, because a blockage in the sump hose between the drum and the pump can cause the same symptoms, and that can't be ruled out without tools. Next: If the machine still holds water, follow the appliance's safe residual-water draining procedure/manual FIRST - opening the pump filter with water inside can release a large amount of water. Let me know what you find.
